speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development what support is available to assist preschools that are grappling with COVID-19 rules and manpower shortage issues as COVID-19 cases rise.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These regular reviews aim to safeguard the health and safety of preschool children and staff, while enabling preschools to manage their operations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The measures also consider the fact that the majority of preschool children are unvaccinated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To keep our children and staff safe, and to enable preschools to keep up with changes to the health protocols, ECDA regularly updates the sector via email circulars and infographics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Preschools can also reach out directly to their ECDA licensing officer if they need help or guidance.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In turn, this gave operators time to review their operational processes and manpower planning to sustain evolving SMMs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, we have streamlined the process to allow preschools to submit details of close contacts directly to MOH so that Health Risk Notices can be issued faster, thereby reducing the period of uncertainty for parents and staff.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The surge in cases due to Omicron has affected many segments of society, and the preschool sector is no exception.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise that a high number of COVID-19 cases amongst staff can disrupt preschools’ operations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In earlier phases of the pandemic, cross-deployment of staff across preschools and across classes within the same preschool was restricted to minimise the risk of transmission.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Where necessary, each preschool may deploy staff across classes or tap on relief staff.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Keeping our preschools safe and healthy is a collective effort.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We advise parents to monitor their children’s health and consult a primary care doctor if their child is unwell.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Children who are unwell should stay at home to rest and return to preschool only when they have fully recovered.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We also encourage parents, whose children are five years old and older and medically eligible, to register them for COVID-19 vaccination to give them better protection.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One is on whether ECDA will provide more support in relations to provision of more ART kits to all the preschools to ease the operating expenses and encourage more people to get tested on a regular basis.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The other question is my concern in relations to a disruption of manpower and whether that will compromise the preschools' adherence to the environmental sanitation regime, exposing the children to the possibility of gastroenteritis cases.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: On the second question on disruption of manpower, as I had mentioned in my main reply, it is a balance we want to strike between maintaining the preschools' operations viz a viz getting the children tested.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We understand that manpower can be a stretch, especially at this time when we have quite a number of preschool staff and teachers who might be down with COVID-19, who might be on medical leave.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We want to be able to empower the preschools, give them some flexibility.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, as I had mentioned in my reply earlier, we do allow them some degree of flexibility as compared to before.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In the earlier phases of fighting the pandemic, our SMMs and restrictions had been quite tight.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Now, we have allowed for deployment across classes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We have also allowed for, in some cases, for example, where manpower is very scarce – as I mentioned, mother tongue language teachers – for them to be deployed across preschools, subject to SMMs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: At the same time, as we move to the endemic phase, we hope that we can also try to alleviate some of the stress that both the preschools as well as families are facing, and that is why we will take Member's first suggestion on board as well.
